reasons.D: Closest satiric play: mixes clipped short sentences with long mock-solemn ones, mock-precise wry asides ('if you please', 'read to from a ledger') and a first-person comic detachment like the passage's.
reasons.A: Chatty first-person rhythm with short punchy lines and a colloquial edge ('so they have got him'), but gentler and more genteel, missing the passage's slangy bite and parenthetical asides.
reasons.C: Comic similes and detached narrator fit, but sentences run long and polished, with a smoother literary register than the passage's loose, jerky movement.
reasons.B: Earnest and reflective, with plain, even sentences and a moral close; little of the passage's irony, slang or comic exaggeration.
